stem: What is the recommended management for a child who has fully recovered from a single, simple febrile convulsion and is otherwise well?

options.text: Admission for a 24-hour observation period and an urgent EEG.
Starting daily prophylactic anti-seizure medication to prevent future episodes.
Treating the underlying cause of the fever and discharging the child if they are stable.
Immediate administration of a loading dose of Phenobarbital to prevent status epilepticus.

explanation: Management focuses on identifying and treating the source of the fever; simple cases can safely go home.
rationale: The primary focus should be on the source of the fever rather than the seizure itself if the child is now baseline.

optionExplanations.A: Simple febrile convulsions generally do not require hospital admission or an EEG if the child is well and has fully recovered.
optionExplanations.B: Prophylactic medication is not indicated for a single simple febrile convulsion, as the risks of medication often outweigh the benefits.
optionExplanations.C: Management focuses on identifying and treating the source of the fever; simple cases can safely go home.
optionExplanations.D: Aggressive anti-seizure loading is unnecessary for a brief seizure that has already terminated.
